title: Sell Mineral Rights in Scofield, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Scofield, UT | Carbon County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Scofield, UT above Carbon County's historic coal seams? We research old deeds and buy coal or gas interests with a fair offer.
heroLead: Scofield is one of the smallest towns we cover, a reservoir community up in the mountains above Price with a coal mining history that goes back to one of the deadliest disasters in American mining.
intro: Scofield sits at over 7,600 feet, up a canyon from Price near Scofield Reservoir, and the town that exists today is a fraction of what stood here when underground coal mining was at its peak. The Winter Quarters mine nearby was the site of a catastrophic 1900 explosion, and the coal seams that made this a company town are still the reason mineral interests exist on paper here, even though almost nothing is actively mined in the immediate area today.

For families who still hold a fractional coal or mineral interest tracing to this area, the practical question usually isn't about current production, it's about whether the interest has any modern value at all, and what a fair number looks like for something this remote and this quiet.

sections.heading: Old coal deeds versus modern gas potential
paragraphs: Scofield-area mineral deeds are often a century old, written when coal was the only substance anyone cared about, and the exact wording matters a lot. Some reserved all minerals broadly, which can extend to any oil and gas potential in the surrounding township; others were narrowly written to coal alone. We read the actual granting language before assuming what an interest covers.

Because this high canyon terrain sits at the edge of the Carbon County coal fairway rather than its productive center, current gas potential is modest, and we're straightforward about that when we value acreage here.

sections.heading: What an inactive interest is actually worth
paragraphs: An interest with no current production and no nearby permitting still has some value, largely as a long-dated option on future activity, and we price it accordingly, lower than an interest with an active royalty check but not at zero. Families sometimes assume a quiet interest like this is worthless and are surprised we're willing to make an offer at all.

We're comfortable buying interests like this precisely because we can hold a small position for years without needing it to perform immediately, something that's harder for an individual family managing dozens of unrelated financial priorities.

sections.heading: Getting the title sorted out
paragraphs: Because Scofield's population has shrunk dramatically since its coal-camp heyday, family paperwork on these interests is often thin, sometimes just an old probate reference or a name on a decades-old tax notice. We do the legwork at the Carbon County recorder's office in Price to reconstruct the chain of title, so you don't need to track down documents yourself before we can quote a number.

faqs.question: Is my Scofield mineral interest worth anything if there's no active mining nearby?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though modestly. We price inactive, remote interests as a long-term option on future activity rather than assuming zero value, and can explain our reasoning before you decide.

faqs.question: I only have a name on an old tax notice, not a deed. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. We research the Carbon County recorder's records to reconstruct the chain of title from whatever starting point you have, even a partial name or old reference.

faqs.question: Does my old coal deed cover oil and gas too?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the specific language. Some early Carbon County deeds reserved minerals broadly, others narrowly to coal. We read your actual deed before making assumptions.
